author: TeIq
content:
Q2 (labeler signing-key custody) resolved after researching Ozone's actual posture.

Ozone ships OZONE_SIGNING_KEY_HEX as a plaintext hex env var in /ozone/ozone.env, read by Node at startup. No encryption at rest, no KMS, no passphrase, no OS keychain, no Vault. That is the security posture every active labeler operates under today — defense is rotation, not at-rest.

Polaris's decision (RESOLVED in doc):
- SigningKey trait with four impls: file-plain, passphrase-sealed, os-keychain, cloud-kms-oracle.
- Labeler profile default = file-plain (matches Ozone; startup logs a WARN identifying posture and pointing at alternatives).
- Bluesky profile default = cloud-kms-oracle (rejects file-plain at startup).
- Key rotation is first-class: polaris labeler-key rotate as a one-command flow; old keys retained in revoked_keys table for historical verification.

Threat-model honesty: encrypted-at-rest modes defend T1-T3 only; only cloud-kms-oracle defends T4 (code-exec-as-service).

Doc changes:
- §B signing-key paragraph rewritten with mode table + rotation discussion.
- REQ-11 (SigningKey trait + impls) and REQ-12 (rotation tooling) added.
- AC-13 (impls exist), AC-14 (startup warning + Bluesky-profile refusal), AC-15 (rotation end-to-end) added.
- Q2 marked RESOLVED inline.
- Out of Scope: TPM/hardware-token modes deferred post-v1; Ozone migration noted as config-rename for the signing key.
